arxiv-2102-03984.title: One-shot Face Reenactment Using Appearance Adaptive Normalization
arxiv-2102-03984.creator: Guangming Yao, Yi Yuan, Tianjia Shao, Shuang Li, Shanqi Liu, Yong Liu, Mengmeng Wang, Kun Zhou
arxiv-2102-03984.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Guangming Yao, Yi Yuan, Tianjia Shao, Shuang Li, Shanqi Liu, Yong Liu, Mengmeng Wang, Kun Zhou. The paper proposes a novel generative adversarial network for one-shot face reenactment, which can animate a single face image to a different pose-and-expression (provided by a driving image) while keeping its original appearance.

arxiv-2103-07884.title: Rare events of a peculiar thermonuclear supernova that precedes a core collapse supernova
arxiv-2103-07884.creator: Ealeal Bear, Noam Soker
arxiv-2103-07884.description: Abstract We study stellar binary evolution that leads to the formation of a white dwarf (WD) that explodes in a thermonuclear supernova at the termination of a common envelope evolution (CEE) shortly before the core of its companion explodes as a core-collapse supernova (CCSN).

arxiv-2202-00418.title: Review of Serial and Parallel Min-Cut/Max-Flow Algorithms for Computer Vision
arxiv-2202-00418.creator: Patrick M. Jensen, Niels Jeppesen, Anders B. Dahl, and Vedrana A. Dahl
arxiv-2202-00418.description: Abstract Minimum cut/maximum flow (min-cut/max-flow) algorithms solve a variety of problems in computer vision and thus significant effort has been put into developing fast min-cut/max-flow algorithms. As a result, it is difficult to choose an ideal algorithm for a given problem. Furthermore, parallel algorithms have not been thoroughly compared.

arxiv-2206-00339.title: Adaptive time integration of mechanical forces in center-based models for biological cell populations
arxiv-2206-00339.creator: Per Lötstedt, Sonja Mathias Department of Information Technology. Uppsala University, SE-751 05 Uppsala, Sweden
arxiv-2206-00339.description: Abstract Center-based models are used to simulate the mechanical behavior of biological cells during embryonic development or cancer growth. To allow for the simulation of biological populations potentially growing from a few individual cells to many thousands or more, these models have to be numerically efficient, while being reasonably accurate on the level of individual cell trajectories.

arxiv-2307-08869.title: Culture, Gender, and Labor Force Participation: Evidence from Colombia We thank Violeta Martínez Calle for her invaluable efforts in searching for all the anecdotal evidence for the study. All errors or omissions are ours.
arxiv-2307-08869.creator: Hector Galindo-Silva, Paula Herrera-Idárraga
arxiv-2307-08869.description: Abstract This study investigates the impact of integrating gender equality into the Colombian constitution of 1991 on attitudes towards gender equality, experiences of gender-based discrimination, and labor market participation. Using a difference-in-discontinuities framework, we compare individuals exposed to mandatory high school courses on the Constitution with those who were not exposed.

arxiv-2402-13984.title: Stability-Aware Training of Machine Learning Force Fields with Differentiable Boltzmann Estimators
arxiv-2402-13984.creator: Sanjeev Raja sanjeevr@berkeley.edu, Ishan Amin ishanthewizard@berkeley.edu, Fabian Pedregosa pedregosa@google.com, Aditi Krishnapriyan aditik1@berkeley.edu Department of Computer Science and Department of Chemical Engineering, UC Berkeley; LBNL
arxiv-2402-13984.description: Abstract Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) are an attractive alternative to ab-initio methods for molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. However, they can produce unstable simulations, limiting their ability to model phenomena occurring over longer timescales and compromising the quality of estimated observables.

arxiv-2501-10316.title: Know Your Mistakes: Towards Preventing Overreliance on Task-Oriented Conversational AI Through Accountability Modeling
arxiv-2501-10316.creator: Suvodip Dey, Yi-Jyun Sun, Gokhan Tur, Dilek Hakkani-Tür
arxiv-2501-10316.description: Abstract Recent LLMs have enabled significant advancements for conversational agents. However, they are also well known to hallucinate, producing responses that seem plausible but are factually incorrect. On the other hand, users tend to over-rely on LLM-based AI agents, accepting AI’s suggestion even when it is wrong.

arxiv-2502-10931.title: D-CIPHER: D ynamic C ollaborative I ntelligent Multi-Agent System with P lanner and H eterogeneous E xecuto r s for Offensive Security
arxiv-2502-10931.creator: Meet Udeshi*, Minghao Shao*, Haoran Xi*, Nanda Rani, Kimberly Milner, Venkata Sai Charan Putrevu, Brendan Dolan-Gavitt, Sandeep Kumar Shukla, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Farshad Khorrami, Ramesh Karri, Muhammad Shafique
arxiv-2502-10931.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have been used in cybersecurity such as autonomous security analysis or penetration testing. Capture the Flag (CTF) challenges serve as benchmarks to assess automated task-planning abilities of LLM agents for cybersecurity. Early attempts to apply LLMs for solving CTF challenges used single-agent systems, where feedback was restricted to a single reasoning-action loop.

arxiv-2503-14387.title: Electromagnetic field solver for QED polarization in super-strong magnetic fields of magnetar and laser plasmas
arxiv-2503-14387.creator: M. Alawashra, J. Benáček, M. Pohl, and M.V. Medvedev
arxiv-2503-14387.description: Abstract Super-strongly magnetized plasmas play a crucial role in extreme environments of magnetar and laboratory laser experiments, demanding comprehensive understanding of how quantum electrodynamic (QED) effects influence plasma behaviour. Earlier analytical and semi-analytical calculations have shown that QED effects can significantly modify the plasma polarization mode behaviour around magnetars using analytical and semi-analytical calculations.

pmc-10546819.title: The Impact of HIV Infection on Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant Chemotherapy Relative Dose Intensity in South African Patients with Breast Cancer
pmc-10546819.creator: Daniel S O’Neil, Oluwatosin A Ayeni, Hayley A Farrow, Wenlong Carl Chen, Georgia Demetriou, Ines Buccimazza, Sharon Čačala, Laura W Stopforth, Maureen Joffe, Michael H Antoni, Gilberto Lopes, Yoanna S Pumpalova, Witness Mapanga, Judith S Jacobson, Katherine D Crew, Alfred I Neugut, Paul Ruff, Herber
pmc-10546819.description: IntroductionIn the South African Breast Cancer and HIV Outcomes (SABCHO) study, we previously found that breast cancer patients living with HIV and treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy achieve lower rates of complete pathologic response than patients without HIV. We now assess the impact of comorbid HIV on receipt of timely and complete neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy.

pmc-10643071.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure induced by antiviral therapy for chronic hepatitis C: A case report
pmc-10643071.creator: Jiang-Li Zhong, Ling-Wei Zhao, Ying-Hua Chen, Ya-Wen Luo
pmc-10643071.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). There have been no reports of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) during treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) with direct-acting antivirals (DAAs).CASE SUMMARYWe report a 50-year-old male patient with CHC. The patient sought medical attention from the Department of Infectious Diseases at our hospital due to severe yellowing of the skin and sclera, which developed 3 mo previously and attended two consecutive hospitals without finding the cause of liver damage.

pmc-12468915.title: Dual PET Imaging with [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-TOC and [18F]FDG to Localize Neuroendocrine Tumors of Unknown Origin
pmc-12468915.creator: Ali Zaidi, Pavithraa Ravi, Ingrid Bloise, Sara Harsini, Heather C. Stuart, Hagen F. Kennecke, Ian Alberts, François Bénard, Don Wilson, Patrick Martineau, Jonathan M. Loree
pmc-12468915.description: Simple SummaryPatients with neuroendocrine cancers sometimes have tumors that spread without doctors being able to find where the cancer started. This is called cancer of unknown primary (CUP). Finding the primary tumor is important because it helps guide treatment decisions.

pmc-12511307.title: Heritability of early seedling growth in Taxus baccata, a declining conifer
pmc-12511307.creator: Igor J Chybicki, Jan Suszka, Katarzyna Meyza, Grzegorz Iszkuło
pmc-12511307.description: In the face of ongoing climate change, understanding adaptive potential is crucial for conserving the functional biodiversity of forests. In trees, early growth influences competitive ability, rendering seedling attributes suitable candidates for adaptive traits. However, determining whether any trait contributes to the evolutionary potential requires proving its heritability.

pmc-12961519.title: Expedited Transplant Allocation Using a Paired Kidney Cohort
pmc-12961519.creator: Miko E. Yu, S. Ali Husain, Emma G. Tucker, Prateek Sahni, David C. Cron, Jesse D. Schold, Joel T. Adler, Sumit Mohan
pmc-12961519.description: This cohort study estimates the incidence of unilateral out-of-sequence transplants, in which 1 kidney is placed in sequence and the other kidney from the same donor is placed out of sequence. Introduction For patients with end-stage kidney disease, kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment, conferring better survival and quality of life compared with dialysis.

pmc-13096902.title: Mechanistic study of inspiratory training in childhood Asthma: Rationale and methods of a pediatric clinical trial
pmc-13096902.creator: Dharini M. Bhammar, Harrison N. Jones, Tarig M. Ali-Dinar, Melissa C. Orenduff, Angel Davalos, Benjamin A. Goldstein, Jason E. Lang
pmc-13096902.description: Asthma is a common pediatric disease of the airways. Obesity among children increases the risk of asthma and is associated with a unique non-allergic asthma phenotype that is highly symptomatic and often unresponsive to conventional drugs. However, the mechanisms linking obesity with incident asthma, more frequent and severe symptoms, and resistance to conventional drugs remain unknown.

pmc-13145307.title: Examination of the Relationship Between Foot Care Behaviour, Self‐Efficacy, and Diabetes Self‐Care Among Individuals With and Without Diabetic Foot Wounds
pmc-13145307.creator: Elif Boz, Eylem Topbaş
pmc-13145307.description: AimThis study aimed to examine the relationship between foot care behaviours, self‐efficacy and diabetes self‐care activities among individuals with and without diabetic foot wounds and to identify associated sociodemographic and disease‐related factors.MethodsA cross‐sectional study was conducted with 120 patients presenting to the internal medicine, endocrinology, and diabetic foot outpatient clinics and wards of three different hospitals.

pmc-13207843.title: Association Between Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio and Early Detection of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in Mechanically Ventilated ICU Patients
pmc-13207843.creator: Ioana Roxana Codru, Mihai Sava, Bogdan Ioan Vintila, Alina Simona Bereanu, Victoria Birlutiu
pmc-13207843.description: Background: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a frequent and severe complication in mechanically ventilated intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Early diagnosis remains challenging, and reliable biomarkers for early prediction are still needed. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), derived from routine blood tests, has emerged as a potential marker of systemic inflammation.

pmc-13287087.title: Oophorectomy‐Corrected Ovarian Cancer Incidence, Survival, and Mortality by Subtype, Race, Ethnicity
pmc-13287087.creator: Nicolas Wentzensen, Camryn Cohen, Summer Harvey, Britt K. Erickson, Megan A. Clarke
pmc-13287087.description: BackgroundMost ovarian cancers are detected at advanced stages, with poor outcomes. Ovarian cancer is heterogeneous; the most common subtype, serous ovarian carcinoma, may originate outside of the ovaries. To inform etiologic heterogeneity, prevention, and treatment of ovarian cancer, we conducted the first evaluation of oophorectomy‐corrected incidence and mortality trends of ovarian, fallopian tube, and peritoneal cancers.

pmc-13288082.title: Tiny caterpillars assess threats by the footsteps of their enemies
pmc-13288082.creator: Emilie Mauduit, Sarah M. Matheson, Jayne E. Yack
pmc-13288082.description: Insects inhabit complex vibroscapes shaped by substrate-borne vibrations from multiple biotic and abiotic sources. One underappreciated topic is how vibrations function in predator–prey interactions. Tiny warty birch caterpillars (Falcaria bilineata) are known to produce complex vibratory signals to defend leaf-tip territories against conspecifics, raising the question of whether vibratory signalling and sensing also play roles in predator–prey interactions.

pmc-13290379.title: Impact of Surgeon Procedural Volume on Outcomes Following Cervical Disc Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13290379.creator: Ben Setaro, Riya Garg, Joyce Wang, Kara McConaghy, Wendy Novicoff, Xudong Li, Stephen C Ludwig, Stephen D Lockey
pmc-13290379.description: PurposeThe purpose of this retrospective matched cohort study was to investigate the impact of surgeon procedural volume on postoperative outcomes and healthcare utilization following CDA. Cervical disc arthroplasty (CDA) is considered a motion-preserving alternative to anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) for addressing cervical radiculopathy and myelopathy.

pmc-13316666.title: Fabrication of a quaternary ammonium chitosan/pomelo peel extract nanocarrier system for tea polyphenol delivery: characterization, stability, digestibility, and release properties
pmc-13316666.creator: Chao Ai, Bo He, Xuanlin Luo, Ruobing Wang, Jingling Kang, Xinyi Li, Wenli Xiao, Zhaohong Zhong, Lei Chen, Xi Xie, Huifan Liu

pmc-13385187.title: Clinical effect evaluation of postoperative complications of papillary thyroid carcinoma based on individualized intervention and prognostic analysis of precision nursing intervention
pmc-13385187.creator: Yu Sun, Gang Pu
pmc-13385187.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to explore the preventive effects of individualized interventions on postoperative complications in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma and their impact on patient prognosis.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted, including 1,595 patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma who underwent radical thyroidectomy.

pmc-13548586.creator: Guihua Yang, Su Liu, Huitian Han, Xueyan Yang, Feng Li, Qiong Wu, Zhiyu Zhao, Fei Liu, Zhifa Zheng, Guangxi Gao, Wenjing Ma, Lina Zhao, Baohua Liu, Zhihong Wu

pmc-13550091.title: The Utility of Machine Learning-Enhanced Developmental Cascade Models in Prevention Science
pmc-13550091.creator: Vanessa Morales, Francisco Cardozo, Raymond R. Balise, Sara M. St. George, Daniel J. Feaster
pmc-13550091.description: Developmental cascade models provide a valuable framework for understanding how risk and protective factors interact over time to shape health and behavioral outcomes. Traditional statistical methods, such as logistic regression and structural equation modeling, have been instrumental in uncovering developmental pathways within prevention science.

pmc-13700401.title: Regional Disparities in the Efficiency of Guangdong’s health service system: A Three-Stage DEA Evaluation Based on Data from 2015 to 2024
pmc-13700401.creator: Yumeng Sun, Qiuyun Li, Shuxian Chen, Li Luo, Qiaochu Lu
pmc-13700401.description: BackgroundChina’s healthcare reform has shifted its focus toward enhancing quality and systemic efficiency, yet significant regional disparities persist. Guangdong Province offers a critical case for examining health service efficiency inequalities due to its pronounced internal development gap between the Pearl River Delta (PRD) and the Eastern, Western, and Northern regions.

uslaw-usc-t13-s224.title: 13 U.S.C. § 224 — Failure to answer questions affecting companies, businesses, religious bodies, and other organizations; false answers
uslaw-usc-t13-s224.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t13-s224.description: United States Code, Title 13 (Census); Chapter 7 (Offenses And Penalties); Subchapter II (Other Persons). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever, being the owner, official, agent, person in charge, or assistant to the person in charge, of any company, business, institution, establishment, religious body, or organization of any nature whatsoever, neglects or refuses, when requested by the Secretary or other authorized officer.

uslaw-usc-t7-s5332.title: 7 U.S.C. § 5332 — Functions of Council
uslaw-usc-t7-s5332.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s5332.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 84 (National Nutrition Monitoring And Related Research); Subchapter II (National Nutrition Monitoring Advisory Council). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Council shall— (1) provide scientific and technical advice on the development and implementation of all components of the coordinated program and the comprehensive plan; (2) evaluate the scientific and technical quality of the comprehensive plan.
